questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India prohibits human trafficking?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 23**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 23** of the Indian Constitution explicitly prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and other forms of exploitation.
 
• This provision applies to both citizens and non-citizens, ensuring universal protection against exploitation.
 
• Under Article 23, acts such as begar (compulsory labor without payment) are outlawed, emphasizing dignity and equality.
 
• Article 23 is enforceable by law, and violations can lead to punitive actions under relevant legislations such as the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956.
 
• This article is a part of the Fundamental Rights section, which guarantees civil liberties to all individuals against state and private exploitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Trafficking:**

 
 
• Refers to the illegal trade of humans for exploitation such as forced labor, sexual slavery, or commercial sexual exploitation.
 
• Globally recognized as a serious crime and violation of human rights under international laws such as the Palermo Protocol.
 
 
 
• **Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956:**
 
 
• A key legislation in India aimed at preventing and combating human trafficking.
 
• Provides measures for rescue, rehabilitation, and prosecution of offenders involved in trafficking.
 
 
 
• **Article 24:**
 
 
• Prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in hazardous occupations such as factories and mines.
 
• Complements Article 23 by addressing exploitation specific to child labor.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Article 23 is a part of the Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the Constitution.
 
• These rights are enforceable by the judiciary and protect against exploitation and discrimination.

questions.question: The Utkal Plains are situated along which part of India’s coastal plain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eastern Coastal Plain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Utkal Plains are located along the **eastern coast of India**, forming part of the larger Eastern Coastal Plain.
 
• The region lies primarily in the state of **Odisha** and is bordered by the Bay of Bengal to the east.
 
• The Utkal Plains are characterized by fertile alluvial soil, making them suitable for **agriculture**, particularly rice cultivation.
 
• This region is known for its major rivers, such as the **Mahanadi**, Brahmani, and Baitarani, which contribute to the area's fertility.
 
• Coastal features like beaches, dunes, and deltas are prominent in the Utkal Plains, shaping its unique geographical and ecological profile.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eastern Coastal Plain:**

 
 
• The Eastern Coastal Plain stretches from the **suburbs of West Bengal to Tamil Nadu**, covering states like Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and parts of Puducherry.
 
• It is broader and more fertile compared to the Western Coastal Plain, with prominent deltas like the **Ganga-Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri**.
 
• The plain is known for its **rich biodiversity**, including mangroves, estuaries, and lagoons such as the Chilika Lake in Odisha.
 
 
 
• **Utkal Plains' Significance:**
 
 
• The region is rich in **minerals** like bauxite and iron ore, fostering industrial development in Odisha.
 
• It is home to cultural landmarks such as the famous **Jagannath Temple in Puri** and the Sun Temple in Konark.
 
 
 
• **Coastal Plains of India:**
 
 
• India's coastal plains are divided into the **Eastern Coastal Plain** and the **Western Coastal Plain**.
 
• The Eastern Coastal Plain is wider, while the Western Coastal Plain is narrower and interrupted by the Western Ghats.
 
 
 
• **Rivers of Odisha:**
 
 
• Major rivers such as the **Mahanadi, Brahmani, and Subarnarekha** support agriculture and irrigation in Odisha.
 
• The Mahanadi River forms a vast delta before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: The Takht-i-Bahi inscription is associated with which region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Takht-i-Bahi inscription is linked to the ancient region of **Gandhara**, which was located in the present-day areas of northern Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan.
 
• Takht-i-Bahi is a **Buddhist monastic complex** known for its historical and archaeological significance, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.
 
• The inscription and site date back to the **Kushan period**, reflecting the flourishing of Buddhism in Gandhara during this era.
 
• Gandhara was a key center for the dissemination of Buddhist art, culture, and teachings, heavily influenced by Greek and Hellenistic styles due to Alexander the Great's incursions into the region.
 
• Takht-i-Bahi remains one of the most well-preserved monastic complexes from the Gandhara period, providing valuable insights into ancient Buddhist practices and architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gandhara Art**

 
 
• Gandhara art is known for its fusion of **Indian and Hellenistic influences**, creating unique representations of Buddhist iconography.
 
• It played a significant role in the development of Buddhist sculpture, particularly the depiction of the Buddha in human form.
 
• The art is characterized by intricate carvings, reliefs, and statues made from stone, stucco, and clay.
 
 
 
• **Kushan Empire**
 
 
• The Kushan Empire ruled over Gandhara during the 1st-3rd centuries CE, promoting Buddhism and trade along the Silk Road.
 
• Kushan rulers, such as Kanishka, were instrumental in spreading Buddhism to Central Asia and China.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Status**
 
 
• Takht-i-Bahi was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **1980** due to its historical, cultural, and architectural importance.
 
• The site includes stupas, monastic cells, meditation halls, and assembly areas, showcasing the monastic lifestyle of ancient Buddhist practitioners.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Monastic Practices**
 
 
• Buddhist monasteries like Takht-i-Bahi served as centers for religious education, meditation, and community welfare.
 
• Monks followed strict routines of study and meditation while adhering to the teachings of the Buddha.
 
• Such sites were funded by local rulers, merchants, and pilgrims who supported the spread of Buddhism.

questions.question: The 'Reclining Statue of Lord Vishnu' is found in which of the following caves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Undavalli caves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "Reclining Statue of Lord Vishnu" is located in the **Undavalli caves**, situated in the Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• This statue is a prominent example of ancient Indian rock-cut architecture, carved out of a single block of granite.
 
• The statue depicts Lord Vishnu in a reclining posture, also known as **Anantasayana**, resting on the serpent Adishesha.
 
• The Undavalli caves date back to the **4th-5th century CE** and were originally associated with Buddhist monks before being adapted for Hindu worship.
 
• The caves are classified as **monolithic rock-cut architecture** and are considered a significant heritage site in South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Undavalli Caves:**

 
 
• The caves are a fine example of **Gupta period architecture**, which reflects the transition from Buddhism to Hinduism in ancient India.
 
• They are multi-storied caves, with the largest one containing the iconic statue of Lord Vishnu in a reclining posture.
 
• The caves were initially built as Buddhist monasteries and later converted into Hindu temples.
 
• The site is under the protection of the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**.
 
 
 
• **Reclining Vishnu (Anantasayana):**
 
 
• The posture symbolizes Lord Vishnu resting on the serpent Adishesha, representing cosmic balance and preservation.
 
• It is a recurring theme in Hindu temple sculptures, signifying the sustainer of the universe.
 
 
 
• **Rock-Cut Architecture:**
 
 
• This architectural style involves carving temples, monasteries, or sculptures directly out of natural rock formations.
 
• Famous examples in India include the Ajanta caves, Ellora caves, and Elephanta caves.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Caves in India:**
 
 
• **Ajanta Caves:** Known for Buddhist frescoes and paintings.
 
• **Ellora Caves:** Famous for Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist rock-cut temples, including the Kailasa temple.
 
• **Elephanta Caves:** Located near Mumbai, showcasing Hindu Shaivite sculptures.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an 'Avanaddha Vadya'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manjira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Manjira** is a pair of small hand cymbals, commonly used in Indian devotional and folk music.
 
• Manjira is classified as an **Idiophone** instrument, which produces sound primarily by the vibration of the instrument itself, without the use of strings or membranes.
 
• Unlike Avanaddha Vadya (membranophones), Manjira does not have a stretched membrane that is struck to produce sound.
 
• Avanaddha Vadya refers to percussion instruments like Dhol, Tabla, and Damru, which use a tightly stretched membrane to create sound when struck or played.
 
• Manjira is not categorized as an Avanaddha Vadya because it lacks the defining characteristic of a stretched membrane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Avanaddha Vadya:**

 
 
• These are percussion instruments that produce sound by striking a stretched membrane.
 
• Examples include Tabla, Dhol, Damru, Mridangam, and Pakhawaj.
 
• They are an integral part of Indian classical and folk music.
 
 
 
• **Idiophones:**
 
 
• Instruments that produce sound by vibrating themselves, without the use of strings or membranes.
 
• Examples include Manjira, Ghungroo, and Jal Tarang.
 
• They are primarily used in folk and devotional music in India.
 
 
 
• **Membranophones vs. Idiophones:**
 
 
• Membranophones (like Tabla) use a stretched membrane for sound production, while Idiophones (like Manjira) rely on the material of the instrument itself.
 
• These classifications are part of the Hornbostel-Sachs system of musical instrument categorization.
 
 
 
• **Manjira in Indian Music:**
 
 
• Manjira is often used in bhajans, kirtans, and traditional folk dances.
 
• Its bright, metallic sound complements vocals and other instruments in devotional settings.

questions.question: The first Law Commission in India was headed by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Macaulay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first Law Commission in India was established in 1834 under the Charter Act of 1833.
 
• Lord Thomas Babington Macaulay was appointed as the Chairman of the First Law Commission.
 
• The Commission was tasked with codifying Indian laws and making them uniform across the country.
 
• One of its significant achievements was the drafting of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), which was later enacted in 1860.
 
• The work done by the Law Commission under Macaulay laid the foundation for the modernization of the Indian legal system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter Act of 1833:**

 
 
• This Act was a landmark legislation by the British Parliament that centralized legislative authority in India.
 
• It marked the beginning of law codification in India and led to the formation of the First Law Commission.
 
• The Act also abolished the East India Company's monopoly on trade.
 
 
 
• **Indian Penal Code (IPC):**
 
 
• The IPC was drafted by the First Law Commission under Lord Macaulay's leadership.
 
• It serves as the primary criminal code for India, covering offenses and their punishments.
 
• Enacted in 1860, it has undergone several amendments but remains a cornerstone of Indian criminal law.
 
 
 
• **Law Commission of India:**
 
 
• It is an executive body established by the Government of India to recommend legal reforms.
 
• The Commission was first formed during British rule and continues to function in post-independence India.
 
• It is reconstituted every few years to study specific legal issues and suggest amendments or new laws.
 
 
 
• **Lord Macaulay's Contribution:**
 
 
• Besides legal reforms, Macaulay is known for his role in introducing English education in India.
 
• His famous "Minute on Education" argued for the promotion of English as the medium of instruction.
 
• He played a critical role in shaping the administrative and legal landscape during British rule in India.

questions.question: Judicial review is essential to:

options.text: uphold the supremacy of the Constitution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**uphold the supremacy of the Constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Judicial review is a mechanism to ensure that laws and executive actions comply with the provisions of the Constitution, thereby upholding its supremacy.
 
• It empowers the judiciary to invalidate laws or actions by the legislature and executive if they violate constitutional principles.
 
• The concept of judicial review is derived from the principle of the separation of powers and checks and balances in governance.
 
• Judicial review safeguards fundamental rights and ensures accountability of the government to constitutional norms.
 
• This principle is integral to democratic governance and prevents arbitrary use of power by any branch of the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review:**

 
 
• The term refers to the authority of the courts to examine the constitutionality of legislative acts and executive decisions.
 
• Judicial review originated in the United States through the landmark case **Marbury v. Madison (1803)**.
 
• In India, judicial review is an essential feature of the Constitution under Articles **13, 32, and 226**.
 
• It is a part of the basic structure doctrine established by the Supreme Court in the **Keshavananda Bharati case (1973)**.
 
 
 
• **Supremacy of the Constitution:**
 
 
• The Constitution is the highest legal authority in India, and all laws and actions must conform to it.
 
• Article 141 ensures that judgments of the Supreme Court are binding on all courts in India.
 
• The concept reinforces the rule of law and prevents autocratic governance.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers:**
 
 
• It is a governance principle dividing powers among the legislature, executive, and judiciary.
 
• Judicial review acts as a check on the legislature and executive to maintain balance.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Judicial review ensures protection against violations of fundamental rights enshrined under Part III of the Constitution.
 
• Examples include the right to equality, freedom of speech, and protection against discrimination.

questions.question: Which Windows OS tool is used to change the system date and time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Control Panel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Control Panel** in Windows OS is a centralized interface for managing system settings and configurations, including date and time changes.
 
• To change the system date and time, users can navigate to **Control Panel > Date and Time > Change Date and Time**.
 
• The **Date and Time settings** allow users to adjust the system clock, time zone, and synchronization settings with internet time servers.
 
• Control Panel has been a core feature in Windows OS since its early versions, providing access to hardware, software, and user account management tools.
 
• In newer Windows versions (e.g., Windows 10/11), date and time settings can also be accessed through the **Settings app**, but Control Panel remains a legacy tool for advanced configurations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Device Manager**:

 
 
• This tool is used to manage hardware devices connected to the system.
 
• It allows users to update drivers, disable/enable devices, and troubleshoot hardware issues.
 
 
 
• **File Explorer**:
 
 
• A file management tool used to browse, organize, and manage files and folders on the system.
 
• It does not provide access to system settings like date and time.
 
 
 
• **Task Manager**:
 
 
• Primarily used for monitoring system performance, managing running processes, and controlling startup programs.
 
• It does not offer options to modify system settings like date and time.
 
 
 
• **Settings App**:
 
 
• Introduced in Windows 8 and improved in Windows 10/11, it provides a modern interface for managing system configurations.
 
• It includes a section for Date and Time settings, offering a streamlined alternative to the legacy Control Panel.

questions.question: The synapse’s effectiveness in transmitting nerve impulses is most critically determined by which of the following?

options.text: The concentration of neurotransmitter and the number of receptors in the postsynaptic membrane
The length of the dendritic arborisation
The presence of myelin sheaths along the dendrites

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The concentration of neurotransmitter and the number of receptors in the postsynaptic membrane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The synaptic transmission is critically dependent on the concentration of neurotransmitters released by the presynaptic neuron into the synaptic cleft.
 
• The number and sensitivity of receptors on the postsynaptic membrane determine how effectively the neurotransmitter can bind and initiate a response.
 
• Neurotransmitter availability is regulated by mechanisms such as reuptake, enzymatic degradation, and diffusion, which directly influence synaptic effectiveness.
 
• Higher receptor density on the postsynaptic membrane enhances signal transmission, while receptor downregulation can reduce synaptic efficiency.
 
• Synaptic plasticity, including changes in receptor number and neurotransmitter concentration, is fundamental to learning and memory processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neurotransmitter:**

 
 
• Neurotransmitters are chemical messengers released by neurons to transmit signals across a synapse to another neuron, muscle cell, or gland cell.
 
• Examples include dopamine, serotonin, acetylcholine, and glutamate.
 
• They can be excitatory (promote action potential) or inhibitory (reduce action potential).
 
 
 
• **Postsynaptic Receptors:**
 
 
• Receptors on the postsynaptic membrane can be ionotropic (directly linked to ion channels) or metabotropic (indirectly linked through second messengers).
 
• The binding of neurotransmitters to these receptors initiates various cellular responses.
 
 
 
• **Synaptic Plasticity:**
 
 
• Synaptic plasticity refers to the ability of synapses to strengthen or weaken over time, based on activity levels.
 
• It plays a crucial role in learning, memory, and adaptive neural responses.
 
 
 
• **Reuptake and Enzymatic Degradation:**
 
 
• Reuptake involves the removal of neurotransmitters from the synaptic cleft by transporter proteins.
 
• Enzymatic degradation breaks down neurotransmitters to terminate their activity in the synaptic cleft.

questions.question: Which Indian city is most influenced by retreating monsoon rainfall?

• Chennai, located on the southeastern coast of India, receives significant rainfall during the **retreating monsoon** season (October to December).
 
• The retreating monsoon (also known as the Northeast Monsoon) is characterized by winds blowing from the **northeast direction**, bringing rainfall to Tamil Nadu and adjoining areas.
 
• Unlike most parts of India, which receive rainfall during the Southwest Monsoon (June to September), Tamil Nadu, particularly Chennai, relies heavily on the retreating monsoon for its annual rainfall.
 
• Chennai experiences cyclonic activity in the Bay of Bengal during this period, contributing to **intense and sudden rainfall events**.
 
• Nearly 48% of Tamil Nadu's annual rainfall is attributed to the retreating monsoon, with Chennai being a significant beneficiary.

• **Southwest vs. Northeast Monsoon:**

 
 
• The Southwest Monsoon (June-September) brings rainfall to most parts of India, while the Northeast Monsoon (October-December) predominantly affects Tamil Nadu, coastal Andhra Pradesh, and parts of Kerala and Karnataka.
 
• The Southwest Monsoon is driven by southwesterly winds, whereas the Northeast Monsoon is powered by northeasterly winds.
 
 
 
• **Role of Bay of Bengal:**
 
 
• The Bay of Bengal plays a critical role during the retreating monsoon, as cyclonic storms often form here, intensifying rainfall along the southeastern coast of India.
 
• Chennai frequently experiences heavy downpours due to depressions or cyclones originating in the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Climate of Tamil Nadu:**
 
 
• Tamil Nadu has a tropical climate, and the retreating monsoon is vital for agriculture, water resources, and drinking water supply in the region.
 
• The state's dependency on the Northeast Monsoon makes it unique compared to other Indian states.
 
 
 
• **Terminology:**
 
 
• Retreating Monsoon: The period when monsoon winds retreat southward, starting from northern India and moving towards the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Northeast Monsoon: Another term for the retreating monsoon, specifically referring to the rainfall caused by northeasterly winds.

questions.question: The role of the Himalayas in shaping India's climate includes all, EXCEPT which of the following?

options.text: Blocking cold winds from Central Asia
Acting as a barrier to southwest monsoon winds
Contributing to snowfall in northern India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Creating convection currents**__.

__
 
• The Himalayas act as a natural barrier that blocks the **cold winds from Central Asia**, preventing extreme cold conditions in northern India during winters.
 
• They obstruct the **southwest monsoon winds**, forcing them to shed moisture, which results in heavy rainfall in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The Himalayan peaks contribute to **snowfall** in northern India, especially in regions like Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and Uttarakhand.
 
• While the Himalayas influence wind movement and precipitation, they do not directly create **convection currents**, which are primarily a result of temperature differentials between the Earth's surface and the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayas' Role in Climate:**

 
 
• The Himalayas influence India's climate by forming a barrier that blocks cold winds and traps warm air.
 
• They play a significant role in the **monsoon system** by obstructing monsoon winds and causing orographic rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Convection Currents:**
 
 
• These are vertical movements of air or fluids caused by temperature differences.
 
• They are a key mechanism in atmospheric and oceanic circulations but are not directly tied to the Himalayas' role in India's climate.
 
 
 
• **Orographic Rainfall:**
 
 
• This occurs when moist air ascends a mountain range, cools, and condenses, leading to rainfall.
 
• The Himalayas play a crucial role in causing orographic rainfall during the southwest monsoon season.
 
 
 
• **Natural Climate Barrier:**
 
 
• The Himalayas protect the Indian subcontinent from the cold Siberian winds, maintaining a relatively warmer climate in northern India.

• **Statement 1 is correct:** The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model and emphasised agricultural development to address food shortages and achieve food security.
 
• The plan focused on **agriculture, irrigation, and land reforms** to rebuild the agrarian economy after independence.
 
• **Statement 2 is correct:** The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), also known as the Mahalanobis Plan, prioritised **industrialisation**, particularly heavy industries, to build the foundation for long-term economic growth.

questions.question: Which type of wave is a sound wave in air?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Longitudinal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sound waves in air are **longitudinal waves**, where the particles of the medium move in the same direction as the wave propagation.
 
• In a longitudinal wave, particles oscillate back and forth along the direction of energy transfer, resulting in compressions (high-pressure regions) and rarefactions (low-pressure regions).
 
• Sound cannot propagate through a vacuum as it requires a material medium like air, water, or solid for the transmission of vibrations.
 
• Examples of longitudinal waves include sound waves, seismic P-waves, and pressure waves in fluids.
 
• The speed of sound in air depends on temperature, pressure, and humidity, with an average speed of approximately **343 m/s at 20°C**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Longitudinal Waves**

 
 
• These waves consist of compressions and rarefactions, with energy transfer occurring parallel to particle motion.
 
• The wavelength in a longitudinal wave is the distance between two consecutive compressions or rarefactions.
 
 
 
• **Transverse Waves**
 
 
• In transverse waves, particles of the medium oscillate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• Examples include electromagnetic waves (e.g., light) and water surface waves.
 
 
 
• **Sound Wave Properties**
 
 
• Frequency: Determines the pitch of the sound and is measured in Hertz (Hz).
 
• Amplitude: Relates to the loudness or intensity of the sound.
 
• Speed: Depends on the medium's density and elasticity.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Waves**
 
 
• Unlike sound waves, electromagnetic waves (e.g., light, radio waves) do not require a medium for propagation and can travel through a vacuum.

questions.question: What provision was introduced by the Sixty-fifth Amendment Act of 1990 for the welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?

__
 
• The Sixty-fifth Amendment Act of 1990 established a **multi-member National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes** to ensure their welfare and development.
 
• This amendment replaced the single Special Officer for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes with a full-fledged **National Commission**.
 
• The commission was tasked with investigating and monitoring matters related to **safeguards provided to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes** under the Constitution.
 
• It also evaluates the progress of various schemes implemented for the **upliftment of SC/ST communities**.
 
• The commission submits annual reports to the President of India, who forwards them to **Parliament** for discussion and action.

• These are historically disadvantaged communities recognized in the Indian Constitution for special measures to ensure their social, educational, and economic development.
 
• Scheduled Castes are communities traditionally subjected to social discrimination, while Scheduled Tribes represent indigenous groups living in remote areas.
 
 
 
• **National Commission for Scheduled Castes:**

• **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes:**

questions.question: What happens if a municipality in India is dissolved before completing its full term?

options.text: The previous municipal council is reinstated.

A new election must be held within 6 months

questions.solution:

__
 
• If a municipality in India is dissolved before completing its five-year term, **a new election must be held within six months**, as per Article 243U of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This provision ensures the continuity of local self-governance and prevents prolonged governance gaps.
 
• However, if the remaining term of the dissolved municipality is less than six months, elections are not mandatory.
 
• The State Election Commission is responsible for conducting these elections in accordance with the constitutional mandate.
 
• During the interim period, the state government may appoint an administrator or a special officer to manage the municipality's affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 243U:**

 
 
• It specifies the duration of municipalities, setting a fixed term of five years from the date of their first meeting.
 
• It mandates that elections must be conducted before the expiration of the term or within six months of dissolution.
 
 
 
• **State Election Commission (SEC):**
 
 
• A constitutional body empowered to supervise, direct, and control municipal and panchayat elections at the state level.
 
• It operates independently of the Election Commission of India.
 
 
 
• **Municipality:**
 
 
• It is an urban local body established to govern a city or town with a population exceeding a specified threshold.
 
• It functions under the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
 
 
 
• **Interim Administration:**
 
 
• Upon municipal dissolution, the state government may appoint an administrator to oversee day-to-day operations until elections are held.
 
• This ensures that essential public services and governance functions continue uninterrupted.

questions.question: The concept of Lok Adalat draws inspiration from the _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ancient Indian dispute resolution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lok Adalat is an alternative dispute resolution mechanism inspired by the **ancient Indian system of dispute resolution**, which emphasized amicable settlement of conflicts through dialogue and consensus.
 
• The concept is rooted in traditional practices such as **panchayats** and public assemblies where disputes were resolved by community leaders or elders.
 
• The modern Lok Adalat system was institutionalized in India under the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987** to provide an informal and cost-effective mechanism for dispute resolution.
 
• Lok Adalats are organized by **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)** and State Legal Services Authorities to ensure justice is accessible to all, especially marginalized communities.
 
• These courts have the power to resolve cases related to civil disputes, matrimonial issues, and compoundable criminal cases, with decisions being legally binding on the parties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**

 
 
• This Act provides the framework for the establishment of Lok Adalats across India.
 
• Under the Act, awards made by Lok Adalats are final, binding, and enforceable as decrees of a civil court.
 
• The Act aims to ensure free legal aid and promote justice for weaker sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Lok Adalat**
 
 
• Cases resolved in Lok Adalats are settled amicably without any lengthy litigation process.
 
• Parties are not required to pay court fees, and if a case is settled in Lok Adalat, the court fee paid earlier is refunded.
 
• These courts are known for their simplicity and speedy resolution of disputes.
 
 
 
• **Panchayat System in Ancient India**
 
 
• In ancient India, village-level panchayats were responsible for resolving disputes through collective wisdom and consensus.
 
• Panchayats emphasized fairness, impartiality, and community welfare in their decisions.
 
 
 
• **Role of National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)**
 
 
• NALSA was constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act to oversee and implement legal services programs across India.
 
• It plays a key role in organizing Lok Adalats and ensuring justice delivery to underprivileged groups.

questions.question: Where are the elements such as neptunium and plutonium found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pitchblende**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Neptunium and plutonium are radioactive elements that belong to the actinide series in the periodic table.
 
• Pitchblende, also known as uraninite, is a naturally occurring mineral that primarily contains uranium oxides and is the primary source of these elements.
 
• Neptunium and plutonium are found as trace elements in pitchblende due to the decay and nuclear processes involving uranium isotopes.
 
• Pitchblende is mined in regions with uranium deposits, such as Canada, the United States, and parts of Africa.
 
• The discovery of neptunium and plutonium was closely tied to research on uranium and its decay products, which are often extracted from pitchblende for scientific and industrial purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pitchblende:**

 
 
• It is a mineral that contains uranium as its primary constituent and traces of thorium, radium, and other radioactive elements.
 
• Pitchblende is black and has a high density, making it a significant source for extracting uranium and its decay products.
 
 
 
• **Neptunium:**
 
 
• It is a transuranic element with the atomic number 93 and symbol Np.
 
• Neptunium is formed as a byproduct in nuclear reactors or from uranium-238 undergoing neutron capture.
 
 
 
• **Plutonium:**
 
 
• It is a transuranic element with the atomic number 94 and symbol Pu.
 
• Plutonium is used as a fuel in nuclear reactors and as a key component in nuclear weapons.
 
 
 
• **Actinide Series:**
 
 
• The actinide series consists of 15 elements, from actinium to lawrencium, characterized by their radioactive nature.
 
• These elements are typically found in minerals like pitchblende and monazite sand.
 
 
 
• **Radioactive Decay:**
 
 
• It is the process by which unstable atomic nuclei lose energy by emitting radiation.
 
• Uranium in pitchblende undergoes radioactive decay to produce elements like radium, polonium, neptunium, and plutonium.

• **Edible Oil Import Dependency**

 
 
• India is one of the largest importers of edible oils, importing nearly 60% of its consumption annually.
 
• Oil palm has the highest oil yield per hectare compared to other oilseed crops, making it a crucial crop for reducing import dependency.
 
 
 
• **Focus on Sustainability**
 
 
• The NMEO-OP emphasizes environmentally sustainable practices for oil palm cultivation to ensure long-term benefits for farmers and ecosystems.
 
• It includes measures to avoid deforestation and protect biodiversity in cultivation areas.
 
 
 
• **Government Support under NMEO-OP**
 
 
• The scheme provides financial assistance for planting material, maintenance of plantations, and setting up oil palm processing units.
 
• Price Assurance Mechanism ensures minimum support prices for farmers, reducing their financial risks.
 
 
 
• **Global Context**
 
 
• Countries like Indonesia and Malaysia dominate global palm oil production, contributing over 80% of the world's supply.
 
• India's NMEO-OP is aimed at enhancing domestic production to compete with these global players.
